sections.html:
Spokane County sits in eastern Washington, and the city of Spokane is its seat and largest community. Around 558,344 residents share about 1,764 square miles, with 241,434 housing units. Beyond the city limits, homes cluster in Nine Mile Falls, Newman Lake, Greenacres, Peone and Veradale.

Owned homes have a median value of $410,700, and 64.5% of housing is owner-occupied. The county is cut into many school districts, such as Spokane Public Schools, Central Valley, Mead, East Valley, West Valley, Cheney, Deer Park and Medical Lake, and the one you live in shapes the school levy on your bill. The Assessor handles about 212,000 real property parcels.

Values come from the Assessor, bills and collections from the Treasurer, and appeal rulings from an independent Board of Equalization. Roughly 56 taxing districts submit budgets each November, which the Assessor turns into levy rates in January.

  • Treasurer: in the Spokane County Courthouse, 1116 W. Broadway Ave., Spokane, WA 99260. Phone 509-477-4713, email treasurer@spokanecounty.gov, open weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • Assessor: 509-477-3698 for ownership, values and exemptions; 509-477-4787 for business personal property.
  • Mailed payments: Spokane County Treasurer, P.O. Box 199, Spokane, WA 99210.

Spokane bills in two halves, with deadlines of April 30 and October 31. Totals under $50 are collected whole in April. When a deadline falls on a weekend or county holiday it moves to the next business day, so for you that means April 30, 2027 or just after it.

The county mails a single statement each year, with one coupon per half. Nothing by March 31? Phone 509-477-4713 or search for the bill on the SCOUT site, because a lost statement never excuses lateness. Escrow customers still get a full statement, and state law puts the duty to see the tax is paid on the taxpayer.

Online (eCheck, debit or credit card), phone, mail and the courthouse all work, and the courthouse has two check-only drop boxes. During April and October the Treasurer also collects on set dates at Spokane Valley City Hall and the North Spokane Library. The online vendor charges 45 cents for an eCheck and 2.65% on cards, with a $1.00 minimum. For mail, only a federal postmark counts under RCW 1.12.070, so a postage meter date is useless. Send it early.

Spring taxes go delinquent May 1 and fall taxes November 1. Either way, interest is figured on the full year's tax.

ChargeHouses up to four units, and manufactured homesAll other real and personal property
Interest0.75% monthly, which is 9% a year, on current-year taxes1% monthly, which is 12% a year
PenaltyNone3% added June 1, then 8% added December 1

Older bills, from before 2023, accrue at 1% per month. The county cannot waive charges if it mailed the statement to an address you or your agent, for instance a closing agent, provided. One hardship waiver exists, for a personal residence where a spouse's, parent's or stepparent's death caused the missed payment, and it requires telling the treasurer and paying within 60 days of the due date (RCW 84.56.025).

To preserve a right to sue for a refund, a payment under protest must be written down and sent along with the payment (RCW 84.68.020). A returned bank item adds a $30 fee.

Each parcel is revalued every year as of January 1, with a physical visit at least every six years. New construction is appraised annually and owners are notified of changes. The target is full market value, worked out from comparable sales, depreciated replacement cost or income methods.

Your Official Assessment Notice shows up in June, yet levy rates are not set until mid-January of the next year, so the notice cannot tell you the final tax. Bills are not capped at a 1% increase either. That cap touches some taxing district budgets, and special levies, banked capacity and annexations muddy it. In a flat or cooling market, assessments flatten too, since they follow sales data.

Send a petition to the County Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year, or 30 days after the Change of Value Notice went out if that is later. Mail it with a postmark by midnight of the deadline or hand-deliver it for a date stamp. It is free, and a letter or phone call cannot replace the form.

  • State specific reasons the value is wrong and include the parcel number, the Assessor's figure and your own estimate. The board will not weigh your tax amount, other properties' values, the size of the jump or hardship.
  • Anything extra must reach the board a week or so beforehand, specifically seven business days.
  • You hear about the hearing 15 business days in advance, and the written decision usually comes in about two weeks.
  • You can settle with the Assessor through a stipulation of value, or drop the appeal by withdrawal.
  • Within 30 calendar days of the decision you can go to the State Board of Tax Appeals, or you can pay under protest and sue for a refund under chapter 84.68 RCW.

The Assessor starts out presumed correct, and only clear, cogent and convincing evidence overcomes that (RCW 84.40.0301). Keep paying while the case is open. Buyers get an exception: the board can meet again after the deadline for a home bought between July 1 and December 31 of the assessment year at under 90% of assessed value.

A senior exemption exists for owner-occupants 62 or older whose household income is under $50,000. Apply with the form on the Assessor's site or call 509-477-3698. New income thresholds start in 2027 under Senate Bill 6162, signed after the 2026 session, and since the numbers are changing, ask the Assessor for current limits.

People retired because of a disability are covered too. After processing, the Treasurer sends you or your mortgage company a corrected statement.

Paying off a mortgage mid-year? Tell the Treasurer so billing details change and a duplicate bill reaches you.

Ask the Treasurer for a written payoff covering every unpaid year ahead of closing, and have the closing agent pay it from the sale money. Interest builds monthly, so the number keeps moving.

Mail matters here. If the Treasurer sends a bill to the address your closing agent gave and it goes unpaid, the county cannot waive the interest, so confirm the agent has the correct parcel number and a forwarding address that works.

The seller normally owes real estate excise tax, payable to the county treasurer when the sale occurs. State rates rise with price. In the schedule for sales from January 1, 2027, one tier is 1.28% between $551,000 and $1,551,000. A local rate sits on top, and the Treasurer can quote the total.

Left unpaid three years from delinquency, a parcel faces certificates of delinquency and foreclosure under RCW 84.64.050. Any payment on past-due tax must first cover the oldest delinquent year with interest and penalties (RCW 84.56.020). Cash sales skip the lender, and the title company can settle with the Treasurer from your proceeds.

faqs.q: When are Spokane County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Each half has its own date, April 30 and October 31, and a bill under $50 is due entirely in April. The next one for you is April 30, 2027, or the next business day if a holiday intervenes.

faqs.q: What if I never received my Spokane County tax statement?
faqs.a: Call the Treasurer at 509-477-4713, or check the SCOUT site, if nothing has come by March 31. A bill that never arrives does not cancel interest or penalty, because paying remains your responsibility.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Spokane County assessment?
faqs.a: The later of July 1 of the assessment year and 30 days after the Change of Value Notice was mailed. The petition is free, and your payments should continue during the appeal.

faqs.q: What interest does Spokane County charge on late tax?
faqs.a: Homes of four or fewer units pay 0.75% a month and no penalty. Other property pays 1% a month plus 3% on June 1 and 8% on December 1. Interest is figured on the full year, beginning May 1 for the first half.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Spokane County house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, when the unpaid tax, interest and penalties are paid at closing. Get a payoff from the Treasurer at 509-477-4713, and sell or pay before three years of delinquency lets the county begin foreclosure.
